summary: U.S. defense officials warned that ongoing budget instability and continuing resolutions threaten to create a 2027 funding cliff for the Golden Dome missile defense initiative, even as initial money begins reaching contractors and commercial providers expand their defense roles. In civil space, NASA completed an astronaut-deployed science instrument for the lunar surface, issued a request for information regarding a moonbase, and bolstered its confidence in space nuclear propulsion following a national laboratory visit. In commercial activity, SpaceX orbited 29 Starlink satellites from Florida, while Rocket Lab unveiled its GHOST portable launch infrastructure and announced that the first launch of its Neutron rocket may slip to 2027. Internationally, Japan successfully launched a navigation satellite aboard an H3 rocket, and remote sensing firm BlackSky secured a multiyear international contract. In astrophysics, scientists built the largest two-dimensional map of the universe to date—cataloging nearly four billion cosmic objects—and the James Webb Space Telescope observed oxygen-rich dust and water surviving near the Milky Way's central black hole. Looking ahead, observers should watch NASA’s planned deployment of high-altitude jets and balloons to study the August 12 total solar eclipse.
